Some ten days after the rally, the first rumours started being circulated in the village that Vojislav Seselj had read some kind of a list of people who would be -- who would have to leave Hrtkovci. So it was only some ten days after the rally. And could you please look at page 3.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The second paragraph. It's been marked. It says one of the pieces of misinformation that was launched was that Ostoja Sibincic was allegedly one of Seselj's men in Hrtkovci and that he co-ordinated the action to expel Croats from Hrtkovci. And then --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then the next marked passage, it says: "As far as I know, he was not a member of the Serbian Radical Party." So this jibes with the document that the Presiding Judge Antonetti showed you yesterday. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Let us now look at the third document. Did you ever hear of a certain Jovo Zunic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: This is one of the Serbs, refugees from Croatia, from Podravska Slatina, and who came to Hrtkovci. If you look at the bottom of page 1, he describes how it came -- actually, he described that he had already left Slatina and then he went to this place called Veliko Gradiste. This is on the Danube in Serbia. Do you know where that is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: When you go from Smederevo along the Dunav -- Danube toward Kladovo one of the places is Veliko Gradiste?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: This is quite a distance from Hrtkovci?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He spent some six months there. He got a job there. He didn't have a house. He didn't have a flat. And he says: "I worked in an agricultural farm, and one day I was called by Milan Fumic, the owner of this house where we were sitting now, and if I wanted to have a house I should go to Hrtkovci to look." Did you know Jovo Zunic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And he says Milan Fumic was a Croat from Hrtkovci.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And he was -- he summoned Zunic to Veliko Gradiste. In Veliko Gradiste he got information from somebody about his house in Podravska Slatina, that he had to leave and so he called him and asked to meet in order that they would discuss the exchange of their houses. And then Jovo Zunic says, I had no choice whether I wanted to or not. I only had one small room in Gradiste, four by four, four of us, two sons, myself and my wife. I didn't even know where Hrtkovci was until I came and saw that, and then when he suggested we do an all-for-all exchange, I said I agree to the exchange but I don't have any documentation. I came without any papers. Whatever I said, I don't have this document, I don't have that, I don't have this. All he said was that that was his problem. When I agreed he said -- and said that I do agree to the exchange, he took out from his pocket all my papers which were prepared in advance. I was flabbergasted. I just stopped and I looked, and he said, Zunic, there are no problems at all for an exchange. You don't have any debts anywhere. He said you just have some utility outstanding debt, utility services.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Your Honours, excuse me. Excuse me. Mr. -- Mr. -- I'm not sure what the point of this is. Mr. Seselj is reading the entire portion of the statement. What exactly is his question? He should put the proposition to the witness and have the witness answer. This is a way of circumventing the ruling -- prior rulings of the Trial Chamber with respect to the use of these types of statements that we get at the last moment that are untranslated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, to alleviate the objections could you summarise what the document states and put your question, please, because if you read all the pages you are wasting your time which is valuable, and this may give rise to an objection by the Prosecution. So you can say Mr. Zunic states this in the document, you summarise what he says and then you put your question to the witness, because the witness actually has the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: VS-067, is this possible that Milan Fumic went to Croatia, learned about this fine house that was abandoned because the man with the family had fled, and then with the help of Croatian authorities got all the paperwork done and then came to the man and said, Let's do the exchange? Is this something that was possible?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your question is whether that was possible?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know if it's possible for something like that to happen or not. I can't know, but perhaps you could ask Mr. Fumic if things proceeded in quite that way. I cannot know whether he was able to obtain all the necessary papers in Croatia that related to the property of Mr. Zunic in Slatina, i.e., in Croatia. I don't know. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. Let's now look at the fourth document. The fourth document is a statement by Zeljko Dosen. Have you heard of Zeljko Dosen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that gentleman came from Platicevo then I did hear about it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He came from Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that man.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He describes here that he and his brother, as Serbs, had to leave Rijeka and go to Italy. Their mother and father remained in Rijeka, who had a visit by Stipo Plejic and his brother Ivan Plejic from Hrtkovci in October 1991. Have you ever heard of Stipo Plejic and Ivan Plejic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And they had all the information about the house in Rijeka and Zeljko Dosen says to a question by my mother where they got information and our address in Rijeka, they said that they received a list of Serbs from the settlement where I was living through the local branch of the HDZ. Is it possible that the ruling party in Croatia, the Croatian Democratic Community Union, took part in looking for suitable Serb houses for exchanges?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Honestly, Mr. Seselj, I don't know anything about that, whether the Croatian Democratic Union received any kind of information about that, whether the Croatian authorities issued any information like that. I really don't know. It doesn't sound likely to me, but I do stand by what I said before.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Since he was living in Hrtkovci from 1991, on page 5 he says something else that is interesting to me. Could you please turn to page 5.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm just doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: We have something marked on that page. He mentions Aleksa Ejic here now, who told him that the president of the Serbian Renewal Movement was in Hrtkovci and that together with Sibincic he had founded an SPO branch in the village, but that Ostoja recently submit his resignation as president of the local board, but he was still in the SPO. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And that Ejic and Sibincic were good friends. Do you doubt what he said here about Ostoja Sibincic's membership in the SPO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. If this or true what Mr. Ejic says here, I cannot really say anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now we have this transcript. Do you have this transcript now of the conversation with Ostoja Sibincic of 60 pages?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't have it yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, I would just like to put one more question. You don't even have to look at the document.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have just received a copy of this transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Ms. Biersay seems to be apologising for something. Let's see why she's apologising.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Directing my attention to the Trial Chamber, we are moving for exclusion of any discussion or presentation regarding this document. This is, I believe if we're talking about transcript 10, it appears to be a transcript of a conversation with Mr. Sibincic by members -- an interview by members of Mr. Seselj's Defence team. It bears a date of 2007. We received this only moments ago and we object to the use of it. We have had this name come up time and time again with respect to this crime base. Mr. Seselj has waited for the last witness, and he waited until the Court had actually commenced, and he delivered this -- this 60-page document in Cyrillic, and we'd absolutely move that it be excluded from any presentation until it has been translated fully, for the Court's benefit in addition to for the Prosecution's benefit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Biersay, we don't even have six witnesses left before the end of the Prosecution case. In legal terms, as far as I'm concerned, this is completed already, because the witnesses will be taking the stand are witnesses of the Court. So the burden of proof no longer rests on your shoulders. That's the first point. Second point, Sibincic, who I don't know, we've never seen him, is mentioned in your documents as a person who was a member of the Serbian Radical Party, and he purportedly took part in the expulsion of the Serbs in that settlement. Therefore, this is in support of your case. The Defence now, with this document he received at seven minutes past 9.00, we have a paper trail of this, will discuss this. I don't know what questions he is going to put. This Sibincic was someone who could have been called by the Prosecution, and now you are objecting. You may have information. If you do, you must mention what it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: What I'm objecting to, Your Honours, is the use of a document that has not been provided to the Court or to the Prosecution in advance so that we can assess it in a language that we understand. Despite the fax line that claims that this was sent today or yesterday or whatever it was, this is a statement taken by members of the Defence team, the accused's Defence team, and it's signed 2007. So my point is that this was purposely held back for the sole intention of surprising the Court, and we think it's inappropriate, and it's on that basis that we make the motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am sorry, but I must once again reassert my position as regards these documents. I agree with the objection raised by the Prosecution, if that weren't clear enough until now, ever since the beginning of this trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I shall ask my colleague Judge Harhoff what he thinks about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Trial Chamber has deliberated on the matter. The Trial Chamber holds, first of all, that this document will not be admitted since the accused has said that he will not ask for this document to be tendered. Second point: The Trial Chamber, in agreement with the Prosecution, feels that it does not have all the information enabling it to understand this document which is drafted in a language that the Judges do not understand, but the Trial Chamber in the majority holds that the accused may put a question to the witness based on this document. He should avoid reading the document and just say, "I have received 60 pages a moment ago from Mr. Sibincic. The latter says, regarding a particular topic," and you sum up in two lines what he has said and then you put your question. That way we don't have a problem. Now, if the accused is lying when he sums up the content of the document, then he exposes himself to a contempt procedure. He would have then forged the truth on the basis of a document. This is just an assumption I'm making. Mr. Seselj, please put your question to the witness. Do not read the 60 pages, please. Otherwise, we will still be sitting here at the end of the week. Sum up what the person is saying regarding the particular point which interests you. You are not going to be reading the 60 pages, are you?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I can read at the speed of light, so I managed to do it. Why is this document so interesting to me? Here Ostoja Sibincic describes his view of all the events in Hrtkovci. Unfortunately, we will never have an opportunity to see him because Ostoja Sibincic died last year, but in 11 places in this statement he says that he was never a member of the Serbian Radical Party --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, I'm sorry, but you're giving us some information which I didn't have. You're telling us that Mr. Sibincic died last year. Very well. This is something that is totally new to me. The Prosecutor, Mrs. Biersay, may have known about it, but we didn't. If he died last year, you can ask to have this document translated and then ask to have this admit pursuant to Rule 92 quater. That is something which our procedure entitles you to do. That said, since he has died, he cannot come, and if in his statement there is exculpatory material, I don't see why you should be prevented from mentioning this.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it's not a good thing that Ostoja Sibincic died. I'm sorry that he died. Secondly, I do not recognise Rule 92 quater, and I will never use it. I don't recognise it even when the Prosecution uses it and the Tribunal accepts it -- the Trial Chamber accept it. It's a matter of the wilfulness of the Trial Chamber and this Tribunal. I just need some confirmation in the cross-examination. I'm interested in what the witness will say when I put to him that in 11 places, and I cannot give you the exact pages, Ostoja Sibincic mentions that he was not only just a member but the founder of the Serbian Renewal Movement in Hrtkovci, that he had nothing to do with the Serbian Radical Party until 2005. I wanted to ask the witness to look at page 10, the last sentence where he confirms that he had nothing to do with the Serbian Radical Party. And previously it was said that he was a member of the SPO in Hrtkovci, and I just wanted the witness to tell us what his position was in regard to that, and I also wanted to show -- I put my question. I put my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... the question, he's got page 10. We've got page 10 as well. We don't know what's in it because we don't understand but your witness -- the witness understands so put the question to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you believe Ostoja Sibincic when he says in 11 places here, and an example is the one on page 10, that he was not a member of the Serbian Radical Party and that he was the founder or a founder of the Serbian Renewal Movement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This question is addressed to me as the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is quite different from what I said. I thought -- and I really don't see any reason why I would dispute the -- or doubt the assertions by the late Mr. Sibincic. Excuse me. I don't have any evidence to the contrary.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Does that mean that you withdraw your assertion that he was a member of the Serbian Radical Party, which is in your statement, and this is something that you also said at the beginning of your testimony yesterday.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning of my testimony yesterday, I said that I thought that he was, but according to these documents which have been presented or these transcripts, it's quite clear that I was mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Thank you. I have now finished with the statement by Ostoja Sibincic and this could have been done without any of these complications, which I think are being created for me here deliberately. Anyway, now you said that after this rally of mine, Aleksa Ejic, as the president of the Serbian Renewal Movement, and he became that after Ostoja Sibincic, offered armed protection. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: According to your statement, he offered two guards every day who would be securing your house 24 hours a day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I believe you. I don't dispute that. What I'm interested in though is how come that Aleksa Ejic had so many armed men so that he could deploy them to guard your house 24 hours a day. If you had two men on two -- on eight-hour shifts that would be six men a day. So you would need to have at least ten armed men in order to do that. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You couldn't do it with less. How come that he had so many armed men to offer just to you, to you and your family? If he had armed men at his disposal, he probably would have needed them for some other purpose. I mean, this would be a sensible thing to conclude, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I really don't know what other purposes he would have had for these men. I'm just saying what transpired between me and Aleksa Ejic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You know that Aleksa Ejic was not working in the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He's not a police official who could send policemen to offer you protection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume that he wasn't thinking of policemen when he made this offer.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Aleksa Ejic was not an army officer, an officer of the Army of Yugoslavia; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And he couldn't deploy soldiers to guard your house, could he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Aleksa Ejic was not an owner of some company that was involved in a personal and facility security, no such firm existed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It didn't exist nor was it known that he had any such kind of firm.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But Aleksa Ejic had available armed men and he could assign a number of these armed men to guard your house 24 hours a day for a longer period of time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct to the extent that he said that he would offer two men which would guard my house throughout that period for 24 hours a day. I don't know whether this was going to be some kind of long-term security arrangement or was it only meant to cover some kind of period of imminent danger. I'm not sure exactly what he was thinking. I don't know whether this was a long-term thing or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, all right, but it was for at least 10 to 15 days, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, possibly he was thinking of such a period.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. But we won't speculate exactly as to the period that he meant. For as long as you were in danger. Are you aware that Aleksa Ejic, as the president of the local board of the SPO in Hrtkovci, was also the founder of the Serbian guard for Hrtkovci?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And that later as a member of the Serbian guard he fought for a while at Boracko Lake?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is something that I'm hearing for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. Did you hear of Pero Sijacki from Ruma?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the first and last name. Perhaps you can give me a little more detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He was a deputy in the Assembly of Serbia representing the SPO. He was a prominent official of that party in the Municipal Board in Ruma. This is your home municipality, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Could you please look at document number 5. It provides some interesting information. His statement is very short but we're only going to comment on a part of it. This is a document marked with the Roman numeral V.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Here he talks about when the SPO in Hrtkovci was established, this was in 1990, who was the president, and says: "The first president of the local board in Hrtkovci was Ostoja Sibincic, and Aleksa Ejic was elected as secretary of the local board. The two of them at that time were on very good terms and they would always come to the meetings of the Ruma Municipal Board together." Have you found it? This is the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then he says: "When Sibincic resigned he was replaced by Ejic." In paragraph 2 Sijacki says: "In early 1993, Aleksa Ejic reported as a volunteer and a member of the Serbian guard which was part of the SPO. He volunteered to go to the front in Herzegovina." Have you found that part?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then he says when they were in the front, the commander in the field was Boro Ante, a major of the army of Republika Srpska, under whose command everyone was. And then he says the Serbian Renewal Movement at that time, through the Serbian guard that it established, assembled and sent volunteers to the front in the Republic of the Serbian Krajina and Republika Srpska, and then he says that 180 volunteers went with them from Ruma, Novi Sad and Sremska Mitrovica. Ruma is your municipality and Sremska Mitrovica is the neighbouring municipality. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Can you please turn to the next page. He says that the Serbian Renewal Movement organised the departure of volunteers and the officials of the party saw them off in Belgrade, at the railway station, and there was a report published and a photograph on the last page of the "Serbian Word." Did you know that that paper existed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It says that the Serbian Renewal Movement published that paper, and he says that it published a story from the Nevesinje front line about the Serbian guard fighting. You can see that, that he says it -- he says that the Serbian Renewal Party was always proud of the Serbian guard and the fighters, and we never disputed the fact that they fought. And he says: "The name of our unit was the Serbian guard and the only insignia we wore on our patches were the emblems of the Serbian guard. We members of the Serbian guard were under the immediate command of Zvonko Smajlic. We were stationed in various huts at Boracko lake and then we would go wherever we were needed." And we're not going to read this anymore, but we can see that Aleksa Ejic was not only an official in the Serbian Renewal Party but that he was also a fighter in the Serbian guard. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is my conclusion then logical? I'm looking at Madam Biersay doing the calisthenics. She keeps getting up and sitting down. So is it true, then, that Aleksa Ejic did have a certain number of the Serbian guard members in Hrtkovci that he could assign to guard your house 24 hours a day, round the clock, not -- not in terms of for 24 hours, but it was 24 hours every day. We don't know how many days. We -- there was some conjecture here that it may have been 20 or 15 days. Is this the only logical conclusion then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the text that you read out to me, the text that I was able to follow, in 1993 Mr. Ejic went to join the Serbian guard. I was not there at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Please, it's early 1993 when, according to Pero Sijacki, he went to the front line to fight and the Serbian guard was established as early as in 1991. You must have heard about the man called Giska. Have you heard about Giska, the first commander of the Serbian guard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Rodzo Bozovic Giska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I've never heard of him, but -- or at least I don't recall having heard of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, if you don't recall, I'm not going to dwell on that any more.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, Judges, Aleksa Ejic was heard here. He testified in open session, but unfortunately I did not have Pero Sijacki's statement then so I couldn't question him about it, but we've already dealt with this whole issue of Boracko Lake, who fought there and all that so I just wanted to comment that here in open session and I'm not going to tender anything into evidence anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Then we have a document, number VI. You heard about Dragan Mihajlovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just find this document. Dragan Mihajlovic, which Dragan Mihajlovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He was the president of the Municipal Board of the Serbian Renewal Movement in Ruma from early 1991 until late 1993. And --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You can see here in the first paragraph that I marked, he says that Ostoja Sibincic was the president of the local board of the Serbian Renewal Movement in Hrtkovci and that Aleksa Ejic was the secretary. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Can you see on page 2 that again this statement has been certified by the court, as have always statements that I tender -- that I use here.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well. So this is just one more argument to support the thesis that you've already accepted in fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, about the question of certification, you know that Ms. Lattanzi has already told you that certification does not necessarily mean recognising the authenticity, and she's perfectly right in doing that. However, I have already asked you and you have not heeded my request. I've asked you if in Serbian law the fact of making a forged certificate is something that is liable for prosecution, and I had asked you to give me the number of the article and the name of the related law, and you have never answered my question. Now, if you were to provide us with this information, then the Judges could take it into account because it means that if somebody submits a written statement may be liable to prosecution if the statement is proven to be forged. And the fact that there is a seal, that the testimony was labelled by an administrative or judicial authority can give some substance to this testimony under, of course, the reservation that it can be forged. So that's what I mean, because each time the problem may arise again with this seal which you mention and that my colleague has referred to, saying that it is not valid for her.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to clarify that on other cases the accused himself has recognised the fact that the seal is there to certify only that the signature is authentic, not the content. So that is the core of the matter. This is a document which has been drafted, one does not know exactly how, which has been brought before a court or another local authority, and here what is certified is that the signature is indeed the signature of the person who has signed the said document and that's all. So it's not about certifying the very contents of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Maybe I should wait with my intervention until the accused have had a chance to respond to Your Honour's question. So -- and I see the accused has his microphone on, so I'll wait for his answer first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Mr. Seselj, I don't want to spend the whole day talking about this. What counts, I think, is the substance.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judges, I have told you several times that the authenticity of the signature is certified. Just as nobody is verifying the veracity of the statements taken by the Prosecution, by the same token, nobody does that in my case. There is the crime of perjury in Serbia just as it exists here. It is very seldom that we see people prosecuted for perjury, and we have seen how many patently false witnesses we had here - of course I'm not referring to our current witness - and nobody did a thing. So this is simply a certification of the authenticity of the signature, the fact that it was precisely that person that gave the statement. Now, as to whether the statement is accurate and true, that is something that is to be decided later, but we now have ten statements that all say that Ostoja Sibincic was a member of the Serbian Renewal Movement in the local board. Had he been a member of the Serbian Radical Party, he would have stood next to me on the platform at the rally. He may have been somewhere in the crowd, but I never met him in my entire life. Nobody has any shred of evidence to prove that I met him at any point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen, for the sake of time Mr. Seselj agrees with Judge Lattanzi so maybe we're making progress.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Which indeed is a good thing, Your Honour. I feel obliged to put on record that the Prosecution is of the view that it does not matter whether or not the statements that the accused is presenting are stamped or not. The fact is that he has not tendered any of these statements and nothing is in evidence, so it would be an error to consider these statements and the contents of them until they have been tendered into evidence. Moreover, as we have seen with this witness, the witness has not confirmed anything else than, yes, it is correct that the statement says this, that, and the other. So there's no evidence presented as to whether or not the contents of the statement are correct. So I put this on record at this stage because I think it is an important issue that will have to be dealt with in the light of the way the accused has conducted all of his cross-examination and in light of the fact that he has handed up quite an array of documents during all of his case. Our position is unless he tenders it into evidence during his case -- his Defence case, he has presented no evidence whatsoever when he has proceeded in this way. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I quite agree with you, Mr. Marcussen. Proceed, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As if -- I am not interested in what Mr. Marcussen has to say, as if he had called any evidence here in the seven years, and he hasn't, just false evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I would like you to look at the remaining three statements. Have you heard about Dragan Trifunovic? He's from Hrtkovci. He still lives there. He was the principal of the school, and he was a member of the Socialist Party at the relevant time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course I've heard about him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He himself claims, as regards Ostoja Sibincic, the same thing that the other people say, that he had nothing to do, at the bottom of page 2, that he had no links with the Serbian Radical Party, that he was not a member. And at page 2 at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What's the number? Is it number 6?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That's Dragutin Trifunovic, at page 2. That's document number VII.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Document number VII. Just a moment. Yes, I found it, at page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: At the bottom of page 2 it says that Ostoja Sibincic was a member of the Serbian Renewal Movement, and it says at the bottom of the page that he was never a member of the Serbian Radical Party and that he had nothing to do with it. Have you been able to find it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What we can find interesting here since he was a prominent figure in Hrtkovci; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as the principal of the school I would agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He was the principal of the school, one of the most respected and prominent people there. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would agree with you that he was one of the best known people there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You can see this thing that's marked on page 4. He claims that Tadeusz Mazowiecki -- have you heard of Tadeusz Mazowiecki?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Was he the Special Rapporteur of the European Community or of the United Nations for Human Rights? That's correct; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, he says that Mazowiecki personally took part in the launching of this whole scandal about Hrtkovci. Can you see that here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And that a reporter by the name of Branka Jovanovic, from the Belgrade radio, told him that that she had this information. Did you hear that Mazowiecki got involved in this whole Hrtkovci affair?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never. This is the first time that I hear something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Could you please look at the eighth document. Do you know Dobrosav Markovic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've heard about him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He says that he was the president and the deputy president of the local commune of Hrtkovci for eight years.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And that the first exchanges of property began in August 1991. Is he telling the truth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the exchanges of houses in August 1991, I know nothing about that, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Can you please go to page 2.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And again we look at the marked paragraphs. He says that in 1991, Ostoja Sibincic and Aleksa Ejic founded the Serbian Renewal Movement and that -- then that the Democratic Alliance of Vojvodina Croats established its chapter in autumn 1991, and that Bela Tonkovic, the president of the party, himself attended this event. Have you heard about that rally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did but I did not attend it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You heard about Bela Tonkovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Now, whether he was there -- well, I haven't heard anything about that. I did hear that there was a meeting, the meeting that you're mentioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you hear about Josip Cindric?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Dobrosav Markovic says that he was elected the president of the local chapter of the Democratic Alliance of Vojvodina Croats in Hrtkovci. And he says that the Democratic Alliance of the Vojvodina Croats in Hrtkovci was a more serious party, much better organised than any other party in the village, and this could be seen from the founding meeting which was attended by about a hundred people, whereas the Serbian Renewal Movement had about seven or eight people and the Serbian Radical Party a bit more. Is that possible?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't tell you anything about the figures. Whether this is possible or not, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And he says that the Serbian Radical Party did not exist at that time in Hrtkovci. Can you see that he said that?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: In the previous question it was not the Serbian Radical but the Serbian Socialist Party.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You can see the paragraph that's marked on the same page.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the same page.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It begins with the words: "The Serbian Radical Party did not exist at the time in Hrtkovci." And now do you know that Dobrosav Markovic moved out of Hrtkovci?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: We had a witness here who testified in public session, Aleksa Ejic, who claimed that we, the Serbian radicals, chased Dobrosav Markovic from Hrtkovci. And he gave this statement to my associates in response to Aleksa Ejic's testimony, and he says: "As regards my departure from Hrtkovci, I have to say that I'm astonished by what Aleksa Ejic said about my departure, that I was forced to leave by the Serbian radicals. I went -- I left Hrtkovci because of my children, so that I could afford them better education, and I offer -- I offered to -- I took the offer of a man who offered me some money for my house. There was no pressure for me -- forcing me to leave Hrtkovci." Is this an acceptable statement to you, that he was not forced to leave Hrtkovci by anyone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't see any reason why it should be unacceptable. I heard that he had moved out from Hrtkovci, and now as to whether it was under pressure or not, I didn't hear anything about that. I even met him in the period following his departure. He never mentioned any coercion -- or, rather, I didn't meet him. I met his wife, whose parents live in Croatia, and I hear and I talked to her and I assume that she would have told me had there been any coercion.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, you can see what happened. Dobrosav Markovic went on TV. You know that the Serbian state TV is broadcasting all -- the whole of the trial, everything that goes on in public session?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. I heard about that. I don't know whether it's the whole of the trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, he saw the trial on TV, what Aleksa Ejic said as he testified, and he got in touch with my associates and wanted to give them this statement when he heard what he said in his testimony. Now we have a very important document. It's not a document that was generated by my Defence team. This is the document bearing the Roman numeral IX. At page 1 is the request of Gordana Pop Lazic, a deputy in the National Assembly, pursuant to our demand that we be given a certified copy of the shorthand minutes of the session of the Assembly on the 14th of November, 2007, and that's what we sent on the 12th of February, just now. Have you been able to find it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You say something in your statement and in your viva voce testimony, you repeated the same thing, that a delegation came to Hrtkovci from Belgrade. We can see that in paragraph 14 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You say that a delegation from Belgrade came to Hrtkovci, that it included Vesna Pesic, and this is when you learned that your name was on the list of people who should leave. I never heard that my name being called out or -- and I never saw a list of people with the names. Some people did see the list of names and they said that it contained my name. You confirmed yesterday that Vesna Pesic did arrive as part of that delegation in Hrtkovci; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: -- there was a debate --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'm unsure, but I would ask that -- just in an abundance of caution that that be redacted for reasons I'm sure the Trial Chamber understands. And I will be happy to explain.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it cannot be redacted. There's no reason for the redaction. It was in public session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Biersay, what is it that you would like to redact? There was a trial that I was not in charge of, the trial of Mr. Seselj about this book. In theory, the trial was made public, and the book must have also been mentioned publicly. A Trial Chamber declared that Mr. Seselj was guilty of having disclosed in this book the identity of three protected witnesses, if memory serves me right. Mr. Seselj has lodged an appeal. I don't know what is the status of the appeal, so for the time being he's presumed innocent as is the appellant, and the appeal is pending. And it probably was the case. I don't think that there was such a thing as a secret trial. If that was explained during the hearings, why should we say today, well, no, all of this must be made confidential. I mean, it's hard for me to follow. What is it that you would like to redact exactly?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj has just described a reference in his book that he has attributed to this witness. It is -- I'm not talking about the contempt trial. I'm talking about him referring to parts of his book that reflect the past statements given by this witness which was exactly the issue at hand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. So you're saying that in the book there's the name of the witness, and so all you have to do is read the book with about the ten names and there is a risk that the witness may be identified. You are right in saying that. I'm going to ask my colleagues whether we need to have that redaction made or not.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in that part of the book the name of this witness isn't mentioned at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: That's not the issue. The issue is not whether the name of the witness was mentioned. The issue is whether there is information contained in the book that tends to identify the witness, and I believe that issue has been addressed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This witness yesterday in public session that was seen by the whole of the Serbian public mentioned Vesna Pesic's arrival in Hrtkovci, saying that he heard on that occasion that his name was on the list of people who should go. This was discussed yesterday in open session, and this is why I want to address this with this witness, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you're allowed to ask the question. The only problem Mrs. Biersay has is that you said earlier that the name of the witness is in the book. That's all. And that, according to me, is where the problem lies. You should not have said that the name of the witness was in the book. Mrs. Biersay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: The information -- he's correct. I -- not the name, the name's not in the book but because of the type of information and attributing it and other information about the witness in the book, that's what tends to identify the witness. So that's what I'm drawing attention to.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, I'm not going to read the book. I mentioned the book in order to tell you how this debate in the National Assembly came to be. Nemanja Sarovic, a deputy in the National Assembly, quoted a part of that book in public. It was broadcast live on TV. He quoted that part of the book where Vesna Pesic was mentioned, and Vesna Pesic reacted as if burned, and she said several times that she never went to Hrtkovci at all, and you can see those parts marked here. That's what Vesna Pesic said in the National Assembly before millions of viewers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, I understand, Mr. Seselj. In the document which is now translated, this is something which shows that Vesna Pesic did not come, and this has nothing to do with the witness we're hearing now except about the fact that the witness may not agree, but that's another issue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is. It is linked with this issue, because this witness said that he learnt that his name was on the list of people to be expelled when Vesna Pesic came to Hrtkovci. It's in his statement, and that's what he testified yesterday in public session. At page 4, could you please look at what is marked here. Vesna Pesic says, "I have never been in Hrtkovci." It seems that you are confusing people here. She told Nemanja Sarovic that he was a liar and she said -- used all other kinds of offensive language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, put your question and we'll see whether through your question there is a risk that the witness may be identified. I'm not able to say that for the time being because you haven't asked your question yet. We know that you have written a book. We don't have the title of this book. We know that you have been sentenced. We know that we have this document which appears to be an official document, and the whole discussion is to know whether, yes or no, Vesna Pesic has come to Hrtkovci. And you would like the witness to confirm or not what he may have said before about the coming of that delegation. Is that what you're trying to establish?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. And I asked the witness to read --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, then please ask your question because unless you put the question, I don't know whether there is a risk of the witness being identified. And if so, then we'll redact immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: From this certified copy of the shorthand minutes of the session of the National Assembly, were you able to see that Vesna Pesic denies ever having gone to Hrtkovci at all, and that the man who says she was there, she tells him, "You're a liar. This is your usual way of doing things. Can you prove any of your allegations?" Can you see that in the marked part or do I need you -- do I need to read all of it to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there's no need.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: She says, I have never been in Hrtkovci in my life. It seems that you're confusing people here. I don't know. Maybe some other person was here and I have never put any foot in Hrtkovci at all, in any place that is called Hrtkovci. This is your custom. You stand at the lectern -- not only you but many of your colleagues stand here and simply say a lie and then if nobody objects, then that's how it is. It goes down in record.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 73. From line 12 to 15. Yes, proceed, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then Vesna Pesic goes on to say, It's like if you blame a puppy for scratching the car. That's your style. Lying is your style. First of all, you lied. You can see that Vesna Pesic is really at the end of her tether. So could you please prove that I commented anywhere anything about Hrtkovci? My name has nothing to do with it. Perhaps you will find some other name, but you will never find my name in anything that is related to Hrtkovci. Have you seen that part?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Does it look to you that Vesna Pesic is really flabbergasted, at the end of her tether?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first of all, it does appear to me --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The witness is kindly asked to speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I could say that this rhetoric is not in line with what Madam Pesic used normally, at least not as far as I know her.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, what does it tell us then? Do you then doubt the authenticity of the shorthand notes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not. I'm simply taken aback by this style, this rhetoric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, in light of that, does it not appear to you that she was really very upset?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, she does appear to be excited and upset because of the claim that she had to challenge here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Can you see in some other places that she repeats that she had never set her foot in Hrtkovci?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Through to the end of the transcript?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you not to leaf through it, not to shuffle the papers because of the microphone. It -- what would you say in this regard --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, Witness. We shall have a break now, but very quickly, in your statement which I have before me, the second statement, the 2006 statement, in paragraph 12 you say that Vesna Pasic was, as you believed, head of the democratic party and that at that time her views were different from those of the socialist parties or radical parties, and you say the delegation came to Hrtkovci. "I was not in Hrtkovci at that time, but my wife told me that a delegation had come." One could therefore conclude that she did come. When this delegation came, you were not there. It was your wife who told you or must have told you. What do you have to say to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's why I would say that -- well, I can only assume because I can't recall with any certainty. Now, whether this was my wife who told me or somebody else. The only thing that I know is that at that meeting or when a delegation from Belgrade arrived, if any arrived, in fact, because this is also challenged here, I couldn't say anything because I did not attend it. Somebody did tell me that Mrs. Pesic was there, but it's obvious then that that person did not tell me the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, if we take into account --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's have our 20-minute break, and the Registrar will tell me how much time Mr. Seselj still has.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The court is back in session. We only have 45 minutes left now. Mr. Seselj, according to our countdown, you have 30 minutes left approximately. I know that the Prosecutor requires five minutes for it's housekeeping issues.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I know the schedule is quite full, Your Honour, but to the extent possible, I wondered if I could perhaps have five minutes to address some brief issues with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Mrs. Biersay will have five minutes, Mr. Seselj five minutes perhaps also, and Mr. Marcussen five minutes. So you should really finish at half past since you had 30 minutes. It is now 1.00. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, from my reckoning, I have 39 minutes left. I kindly ask you to ask your own Legal Officer how much time I have left precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Registrar will let me know how much time you have left. Please proceed. Mr. Seselj, let me remind you that the Trial Chamber had handed out a decision and stated that the objections could be taken off your time, just for your information.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, then, if you're taking time from my allocated time on account of objections, it's not fair. All my objections were to the point, and you're not deducting time from Mrs. Biersay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. VS-067, we were talking about Vesna Pesic now during the break. I was puzzled by what you'd said, namely that what Mrs. Vesna Pesic said at the national parliament was not like her.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said it was not her style.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And you are familiar with her style?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I had heard her saying, and that's not much because I'd left Serbia, Vesna Pesic was always moderate and calm.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And what mental state does a person have to be in, a person like Vesna Pesic, in order to react like that in the parliament, at a session that is broadcast to millions of viewers, to blow her fuse completely? She must have been in a difficult mental state. I don't mean any kind of sickness, but I mean a high degree of irritation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: She was very hard-hit by an incident of slander that she been in Hrtkovci and involved in some sort of scandal, whereas she had never been in that place.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether she had understood that as slander or simply an untruth, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, you know what it's like when somebody says untrue -- somebody says something untrue about you. It's slander. It's defamation, and that's how she understood it, obviously. But she thought it came from the Serbian Radical Party, that they had invented, made up, her visit to Hrtkovci. That's what it was all about, wasn't it? I see that you seem embarrassed yourself, and I quite understand.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm embarrassed inasmuch as my statement given to the investigators may be wrong in that passage. That's why I could be embarrassed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you agree that both your statements to OTP investigators and your evidence yesterday -- would you please stop shuffling the papers, because we can hear it amplified. Do you agree that the two statements you gave to the OTP investigators and the evidence you gave yesterday is full of things that you had heard from other people, and you're not even able to name those people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose you mean mainly the passages where I said to the investigators that Mr. Sibincic had been a member of your party and what I stated about the arrival of Mrs. Pesic to Hrtkovci. Do you mean that?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, there are many things you say you heard from other people, but you don't know who exactly. You said you heard from someone you were on a list.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I heard about that. Whether I was really on the list, I never received any confirmation by way of reading the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes, but you ascribe that list to me. You say that I'm supposed to have read that list at the rally.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not what I'm saying. That list could have been given to you. You didn't necessarily make the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But you take it for granted that the list existed. Somebody gave it to me, and I read it out.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say you read it out. I said that some names were read out from a list. Whether they were really read out or whether they were read out by you, I never made any claims one way or another.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I told you that Mr. Zilic, the secretary of our board, read out the names of people who were no longer living in Hrtkovci and who were allegedly part of the Croatian Home Guard, a paramilitary formation. That's what they heard, and that's what I put to you. Have you heard of Blagoje Dudic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Blagoje Dudic, with a D? No. No, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He is from Hrtkovci. On the 17th of January, 1992, he came to Hrtkovci from Zagreb. He had been expelled from his own house. His house had an area of 164 square metres, and he had to swap with a man in Hrtkovci. Have you got this document that I received at 1342 hours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the second page of that document it says that when he came to Serbia, on the 17th of January, in Hrtkovci there was no board of the Serbian Radical Party. He became a member in Ruma. He gives the number of his membership card, and he says that the Municipal Board of our party in Ruma gave approval that a local board be established in Hrtkovci, and ten members of the Serbian Radical Party gathered, established the board and elected him chairman, and they decided to hold a rally in May. He also says they invited him to the come to the rally -- they invited me to come to the rally because it was a major holiday, St. George's Day. You know why I decided to put this to you? Because he describes in the second highlighted paragraph how the police guarded the rally, how they provide security. You know that every rally, every gathering had to be announced to the police. You know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And everyone had to give at least 48-hours' notice. And he describes that a couple of hours before the rally the commander of the police station in Ruma came to his yard, Toma Milic [phoen]. You know him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He asked him about the organisation of security, and Dudic answered that the rally had been announced properly, and they expected the police to provide security at the rally, like they do for all other citizens. And then the police commander said what if an incident happens, and Dudic answered, "Then we are going to grab you by the neck, as a policeman." And then I'll read: "After that, Milic called for the police to come and they came several hours later, in full equipment with gas masks, and they provided security for the entire rally until the end. Dr. Seselj came directly to the rally. After the rally he had to move on immediately, and to my great regret, we had no opportunity to talk with him before or after the rally." Since you say you did not attend the rally yourself, do you know that a large number of policemen in full equipment provided security?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, Dudic said they did. Where were you at the time of the rally of the Serbian Radical Party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Hrtkovci.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Were you far away from the venue of the rally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rather far away.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You were not able to hear the public address system at the rally or the music before the rally, none of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was far enough not to be able to hear any of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You said something else in your statement that's very interesting, and you repeated that yesterday in the courtroom in open session, namely that your ancestors were Albanians. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Albanians are the ancestors of all the people in Hrtkovci who later declared themselves as Croats, almost all of them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly a part of the population.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I am rather well read about this, and you said that your ancestors, Albanians, settled in Hrtkovci following the Carnojevic leader who led a lot of the Serbian people from Austria. You say that -- in fact, many of your ancestors were killed in Valjevo by the Ottoman Turks who caught up with them. You know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And your Albanian ancestors came to Hrtkovci and Nikinci, to a Serbian area, and they lived along with the Serbs like brothers. Albanians, Christians, always had brotherly ties with Serbs.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say they lived in harmony.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Although you were Catholic and most of the Serbs around you were Orthodox Christians; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And your ancestors became Serbified, so to speak. They forgot the Albanian language and became Serbs. You lived there as an ethnic group for 300 years.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, approximately that long.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But certainly in the 20th century something happened. They forced you to declare yourselves as Croats suddenly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not when it happened. My ancestors declared themselves as Croats, perhaps even as early as the beginning of the 20th century, not towards the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I didn't say towards the end of the 20th century. I said early 20th century, and I suppose as an intellectual you know that. It was after year 1900, after the first Croatian Catholic Congress in Zagreb. You heard about that Congress?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Catholic bishops made the decision at that time that all Catholics who speak the Serbian language are of Croat nationality, and that's the beginning of this Catholic policy. And then gradually they started forcing you to declare yourselves as Croats, although you had originally arrived as Albanians, and you lived rather well in a Serbian environment as Albanians for 300 years. You enjoyed a good life.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, based on what my grandfather used to say, and my father, I'm not aware that any problems existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You know from history that the last Ottoman siege of Vienna was in 1683; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And it lasted seven years, and the Polish King Jan Sobieski broke down that siege?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And in a big counter-offensive, the Austrian army expelled Ottomans from Hungary and Slavonia, entered Serbia and went as far south as Skopje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That's when our Serbian ancestors and your Albanian Christian ancestors took up arms to help, and since the main General, Piccolomini, fell victim to plague and died, the new Austrian commander was not able to stop the Ottoman counter-offensive.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not the information that I have, this withdrawal of the Austro-Hungarian empire.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It was not Austro-Hungarian empire. It was just Austria.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Austria and some other countries that were against the idea that Austria should go as far as the Adriatic Sea.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, the consequence of this big Vienna war was that the Austrian army expelled all the Muslims from Hungary, Vojvodina and Slavonia; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether they were expelled or they withdrew, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, both happened. Large numbers pulled out with the Ottoman army, and a large number was expelled. We can agree on that. Do you know that at that time there came a massive resettlement, including of your ancestors.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean Serbs moved in to your area.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes. Large numbers of Serbs came under Carnojevici. Have you heard Eugene of the Savoie, Eugene of the Savoie, a great commander of the Austrian army. In 1690, with the Austrian army he entered Bosnia, came all the way to Sarajevo, set it on fire. You know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about the torching of Sarajevo, but I do know about this great infiltration of the Austrian army.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And when he pulled out of Bosnia, a large number of Bosnian Serbs, Catholics and Orthodox alike, joined him, and he settled them in Slavonia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to be quite frank, Mr. Seselj, this is the first time that I hear about something like at that but I'm not challenging it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The Sokci minority, they are Catholics who live in Vojvodina, and they say that they are Croats. That's how they say.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if they're of Serbian origin or not, but I do know that they now declare themselves as Croats, but again I'm not challenging you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You heard about the Bunjevac minority?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It's a separate ethnic group that it -- it has its own tradition and culture.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the north of Backa.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes, in the north of Backa but some of them lived in Lika too.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The speakers are kindly asked to speak one at a time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that Bunjevci are originally from the Neretva valley, from the Buna river valley, in fact, in Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, the name Bunjevci would indicate that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And Mr. Seselj again, please observe a small pause between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We will make pauses.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You know that the Turks governed Lika at the time of the greatest expansion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And the Austrian army expelled the Turks from Lika; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But unlike in Hungary, Vojvodina and Slavonia, where Muslims pulled out, too, or were expelled, quite a few of the Lika Muslims remained in Lika. You are familiar with that, are you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is the first time that I hear something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then they had to convert by force. They had to convert to Catholicism for the most part, but some of them took Orthodox religion. For instance, you have Orthodox people from Lika whose last name is Atlagic, a Muslim last name.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And do you know that in the first half of the 18th century --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, we've had situations like this before where the accused is cross-examining a witness on things which at best are peripheral and then towards the end of his time he comes to points that seem more essential to the matters here. So I would suggest that maybe the accused be advised to get to the point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, we are -- we control the usefulness of your questions. In other words, the questions you ask are intellectually speaking interesting but in light of the indictment of lesser importance. Your time and ours is extremely valuable, so if you put questions and the answers are "I don't know but I don't deny it," you know, this can go on forever in light of your knowledge of historical events which the witness does not share so he cannot contradict you and he will just say "yes" in reply. So if you just wish to repeat what we -- you have already said, we know that already. So why should you insist further?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, if you've allotted time to me, I am trying to use that time to the best of my ability, as best as I can, but if I have to keep justifying why I ask some questions, in a very proper way if I am engaged in an intellectual dialogue with this witness who is way above the intellectual level of the witnesses we have had so far here, and if the witness himself said that the ancestors of the Croats who live in Hrtkovci today came as Albanian Catholics together with Serbs, he opened up the possibility for me to pursue this line of questioning, to clear this things up, things that are important for my defence, because I think they are important, and I don't have to notify either the Prosecution or the Trial Chamber why I deem something to be important for my defence. The Prosecution has been asking really peripheral, nonsensical questions, wasting our time and nobody's warning them. This is important for the key argument of my defence case. I have only one question of this sort and then I will finish this chapter, if you allow me to. If not, then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please proceed if you have a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Since you are an educated person, of course you're not an historian but I assume that your knowledge is deep there too, have you heard that in the first half of the 18th century, so in 17 -- around 1725, that all the Bulgarians who were Catholics moved out of the Bulgarian areas under Turkish government and moved to the area of Subotica, what today is Subotica. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. Mr. Seselj this is the first time that I hear something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And their descendants are forced to declare themselves as Croats.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I've never heard about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So today they are turning Bunjevac -- the Bunjevac people, who are of Serbian origin but they have their own separate culture and tradition, and Bulgarians into Croats, just as they turned you Albanians into Croats in Hrtkovci. So is this a similar process? If what I have been putting to you is correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether the Croats exerted any pressure on my ancestors to declare themselves as Croats, well, I really don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: No. It is my argument that this was not done by the Croats but by the Roman Catholic Church.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the Roman Catholic Church, whatever. Whether it insisted on them declaring themselves as Roman Catholics or -- or, rather, as -- in terms of their ethnic background, I really don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know in the former Yugoslavia in early 20th century there were about 1 million Serb Catholics living there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is the first time that I hear something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, if that's the case, we're not going to dwell on that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I please be given the remaining time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it's 1.30. You have five minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I have a document here that was submitted to me by the Prosecution. It's an excerpt from one of my books. The number is 0626-4255. It's a statement by the wife of the man with whom you exchanged houses. I'm not going to mention the name because that might disclose your identity.
