You have it in the bundle of documents that you received, and the Registrar can help you. It's not my document, so it doesn't bear any Roman numerals. The number on the document is 0626-4255. Have you been able to find it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm still looking.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may, this was inserted in your binders. It's an extract from Mr. Seselj's book.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will not specify the title of the book because we want to protect the identity of the witness. We don't want to be bothered by going into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Have you been able to find it, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But you can tell me what it's all about.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I would like to elicit your comments on some of the parts therein, the parts that I highlighted. The statement has been translated into English and I cannot be criticised on any account now. She describes how her entire family, her husband had died in the meantime, was forced to leave Podravska Slatina in order to save our lives. This is what she said.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't -- I don't have it. I don't have it, but I'm listening to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to be reading it because the Judges and the Prosecutors can follow it in English. "We were very frightened. First a rich local man was killed. He was the only glassmaker in the area where lots of things were being constructed. He was killed at the edge of the village, and then arrests occurred daily. One day they would arrest this man. The next day they would arrest another. And it became obvious that we could no longer live there and that we had to flee." Have you heard about this kind of horrible persecution that the Serbs suffered at the hands of the Tudjman regime in Croatia and that this was the reason why they had to flee?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard that pressure was exerted on some of the Serbs in an effort to make them move out of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you hear that some Serbs were killed in the process?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether there were many of them, but I did hear that some were killed indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, let us contrast this with the situation that you faced. It was probably not very pleasant for you when this huge massive Serb refugees arrived in Hrtkovci, and you were not very happy when you heard about me advocating retortion. I'm quite aware of the fact that it wasn't pleasant for you, but we in Serbia did not kill any Croats. There was one murder, but the perpetrator was prosecuted. Stefanac was killed and it was an ordinary crime. He was not killed because he was a Croat. You know that his murderers were prosecuted.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what was the motive for his murder.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The speakers are kindly asked to speak one at a time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, we have evidence here. I called evidence here, and I also wrote in my book about the sentences they received and so on. I'm not going to maltreat you with that. We have no evidence that the authorities arrested Croats and exerted pressure on them in this manner.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about any such cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know about any cases where Croats were fired simply because they were Croats, if they worked in state-owned companies or in the civil service or public services?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any such knowledge up until the time when I lived there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So the wife of the man who exchanged his house with you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I must cut you off here for a shortage of time. Mrs. Biersay, can you please be as quick as you can. We'd like Mr. Seselj to be able to ask some further questions if he has any.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. You'd like me to do -- to ask questions now.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, during his cross-examination, specifically at provisional page 19 of the transcript, line 15, Mr. Seselj asked you whether or not you were aware of cases that -- where the police intervened, where refugees moved into houses that were occupied by people from Hrtkovci. Do you remember that series of questions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And you said that there were cases of that happening. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Seselj didn't ask you to describe those cases, but could you please describe that for the Trial Chamber, and please, if you think the information will identify you, please let us know and we'll request to be moved into private session. So what cases are you aware of, and can you discuss it in public session?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can. I can. I would only perhaps insist on not naming names. Is that acceptable?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know of a few cases where the police was called, and after they came, the police either prevented people from being driven out of their homes or they did not succeed, either because they did not arrive in time, or -- I cannot think of any other reason. They did not arrive in time.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I don't want you to give the name, but did you have a family member who was, in fact, forced out physically from his house? Did you have such a family member?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, an uncle of mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now I'd like to address the last thing. Are you aware -- well, first let me back up. You have been asked lots of questions about Ostoja Sibincic. Now, in your testimony, what I understood you to be saying was that based on the information that you had at the time, you believed him to be associated with the Serbian Radical Party. Am I correct in understanding it that way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Your understanding is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Are you aware that in August of 1992, Mr. Seselj held a -- that there was a press conference held by Mr. Seselj in which he demanded that Ostoja Sibincic and others arrested in Srbislavci, former Hrtkovci, be immediately released? And that was in August of 1992. Are you aware of that press conference at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is the first I heard of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And for the record that would be 65 ter 1559. Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Mr. Seselj, for the sake of fairness, do you have any questions to put to the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, as far as this conference is concerned, it really makes no sense that it was not provided by Mrs. Biersay in the file.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Objection. What does he mean by it wasn't provided in the file? It's a 65 ter number that's accessible in e-court, and the Court has it in a language it can understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, do you have any questions to the witness about the Sibincic arrest in which you may have -- you are said to have intervened to get him released?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have something to say about this first part. The fact that I interceded on his behalf to have him released, I would do that again. But the fact that I want someone to be released because he's being politically persecuted does not mean that the man belongs to my party. It's a nonsensical question. Why would I bother about that? Another point by Ms. Biersay is important.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you know of any case where a Croat was expelled from Serbia, where the state authorities forced him or her to leave and leave their property behind? Not cases where people felt uncomfortable and then decided to swap properties. Everybody would feel uncomfortable if thousands of refugees flowed in, Serbs and Croats alike. But do you know of any case where a Croat or a Croat family were expelled by a decision of the state authorities, they had to leave their property behind and go to Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well. Another short question. Is it obvious to you that an incomparably greater number of Serbs had to leave Croatia than Croats who had to leave -- or who left Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you take into account the numbers that you quote, then it's obvious.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And under those circumstances, when an exchange of property takes place, is it obvious that Croats who swap property with Serbs from Croatia are much better placed to choose and to bargain than the huge masses of Serbs who left Croatia because they were persecuted or killed and had their houses bombed? Is it obvious that you Croats had a much larger choice than Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you could say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Isn't then a logical consequence that the Croats who were swapping property had a much better deal of it than Serbs, because they could pick and choose? Maybe some of them made mistakes and made wrong choices, but isn't that a logical consequence of the situation on the market? The supply, the Serbs who were offering their property for exchange, were much more numerous than the Croats.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-067 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that's logical.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I'm happy with your testimony. I think it was fair.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I'd like to thank you on behalf of the Trial Chamber for coming to bring your testimony. You may now leave the office in which you're sitting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now before I quickly give the floor to Mr. Marcussen, the Trial Chamber announces that next week we shall not have a witness in light of medical problems that some of them have, but the following week we will have a witness, and the week after that we shall be sitting in the afternoon. Very quickly now, Mr. Marcussen, if you may, because my colleague and myself, Judge Harhoff and myself, in a few minutes are dealing with another case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. There were at the -- Your Honour's questions at the beginning of the testimony of the witness were very much based on the statements that the witness had given to the Office of the Prosecutor, and I wonder whether for the completeness of -- the complete understanding of those parts of the testimony of the witness it would be appropriate to admit those statements into evidence, and I'm therefore suggesting to tender those statements into evidence. That was my first point. My second point is at page 56, beginning at line 18 today, the issue came up as to the current status of the case, and it was said that the remaining witnesses were Court witnesses and that the Prosecution no longer had a burden of proof. The Prosecution's position is that the Prosecution case is not closed. The Prosecution hasn't closed its case, and we will be presenting further evidence in the case. And of course, and I'm sure this might be either a translation issue or simply just in the heat of the battle, but the burden of proof obviously rests on the Prosecution until the end of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. What else do you have? Very quickly. This -- I'm very interested to know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: It's at page 54, line 16.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is it that you're going to present? What further elements do you intend to present as you no longer have any witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: We're going to tender further Prosecution exhibits. There will be further motions, and the remaining witnesses are still being presented as part of the Prosecution case. The Prosecution's presentation of evidence isn't closed. That's my point. Now, the last point --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I quite agree with you on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I have been advised that it would be maybe -- another point. It would maybe advisable that C -- Exhibit C-20, which is the pseudonym sheet of the witness, should be placed under seal. It was not yesterday. And then my -- my very last point, if we could move very briefly into closed session, Your Honours, or private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, please, private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will not take into account what Mr. Marcussen has just said, because it has nothing to do with this Trial Chamber but another Trial Chamber. Secondly, I oppose strenuously the admission of statements that were drafted by the Prosecution and signed by this witness. It is contrary to every procedural rule, be it in common-law or in continental-law systems. We had a witness who testified viva voce here, and this statement cannot be admitted into evidence. If you happen to admit it, then it will be yet another instance in which my procedural rights are being violated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I have said, normally speaking we will hear a witness in two weeks' time. I hope he can come. There are very few witnesses left. We have difficulty bringing them here. We will keep you abreast on a day-to-day basis. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 2nd day of March, 2010, at 2.15 p.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.49 p.m.,
